subject: Post-call: deployment selection & cost follow-up (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment selection & cost follow-up (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Olivia — thanks again for taking time today. Short recap and next steps from our discovery so your execs and procurement have a clean decision path.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary workload: customer-facing summarization + retrieval-augmented generation for enterprise customers (legal docs).
- Current monthly tokens: ~75M input+output currently (prototype) with expected growth to 400M monthly within 9 months as you ramp.
- Peak concurrency: spikes up to 350 qps for short windows during report runs.
- Data sensitivity: PII in documents; need encryption at rest, audit logs, and a contractual commitment to data isolation.

Deployment options we discussed (tradeoffs):
1) Hosted API (fastest): pay-as-you-go per-token, Redwood-managed models and ops. Good for quick launch and minimal ops. Cost-effective at low to medium steady volume but can be more variable at high token velocity.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly reserved GPU pools (committed throughput) — predictable unit costs for steady high throughput and prioritized latency/SLA. Better at scale if you can commit to a baseline.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed network, on-prem image or VPC private control plane. Maximum isolation and control; pricing is subscription + infra + support. Best for strict compliance / data residency.

Questions we need to finalize pricing/commit recommendation: please send the simple usage snapshot (we attached a template csv) with:
- 30-day peak tokens/day and typical day tokens/day
- Percent of calls that need sub-2s p95 latency
- KV cache hit rate expectations (or whether you expect many long context sessions)
- Any hard constraints on data residency or on-prem requirement for the first 12 months

Pricing signal + initial recommendation (from our side):
- If your baseline expected monthly tokens < 200M and you want low operational overhead, start Hosted; we can add burst controls and a cost cap while you ramp.
- Between 200M–800M monthly tokens with predictable baseline, Dedicated reserved capacity often wins on dollars-per-token and latency SLOs. Typical commit structures are 6–12 months with commit discounts.
- If procurement/legal require private control plane or on-prem within 3 months, we should move to Private evaluation now. That has up-front integration and SSO/KMS work (we can provide a statement of work).

Next steps (suggested timeline):
1) Olivia: send the attached usage snapshot populated by Tue, May 4 (we can use that to run a short TCO model).
2) Marissa: prepare 2 pricing scenarios (Hosted incremental, Dedicated 12-month commit) and a delta table of costs + projected savings vs time.
3) Hannah: introduce procurement/legal threads if Private is required.

Attachment: streamline_usage_snapshot_May2027.csv (template)

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick 30-minute follow-up after we see your usage.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment selection & cost follow-up (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hannah — thanks for the clear recap. We did a quick export and attached a filled snapshot (see csv). Quick answers to your questions below; procurement loops in on Friday.

- 30-day peak tokens/day: 35M (peak day during pilot)
- Typical day tokens/day: 6–9M
- Sub-2s p95 requirement: about 25% of calls are user-facing and need sub-2s p95; the rest can be background.
- KV cache hit rate: expect around 40% once we tune retrieval; many sessions are long (3–8k tokens) for multi-document summarization.
- Residency: must remain in US-region data centers for now; on-prem is not mandated immediately but procurement will ask about Private option.

Procurement note: if we move to a committed model, pricing will need to be locked for 12 months and we'll need SOC2 + audit log access for evaluation (we noted Redwood has those). We are aiming for a decision by mid-June.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@streamline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment selection & cost follow-up (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Thanks Olivia — got the snapshot, this is helpful. I ran a quick back-of-envelope TCO for two scenarios and pasted the highlights below. I can produce a formal spreadsheet if you'd like.

Scenario A — Hosted API (pay-as-you-go)- Assumptions: 400M tokens/month steady by month 9, 40% cache hit, per-token rate = $0.0009/input+output blended (includes model tier and streaming).- Estimated monthly bill at 400M tokens: ~$360,000- Pros: no commit, rapid onboarding, Redwood handles scaling.- Cons: bill variability, slightly higher p95 tail due to multi-tenant queues during peaks (we can mitigate with priority tiers).

Scenario B — Dedicated (12-month commit)- Assumptions: baseline reserved capacity that handles 250M tokens/month, with burst capacity for peaks. Effective blended unit cost at commit = $0.00045/token after discounts and dedicated throughput efficiencies.- Committed monthly cost (baseline): ~$112,500 (covers 250M tokens equivalent) + overage at a reduced per-token rate.- Pros: predictable unit cost, latency SLOs, preferred capacity during spikes.- Cons: requires a commit and a short on-boarding plan for reserved pools (2–4 weeks).

Preliminary recommendation: If Streamline expects to sustain >200M tokens/month within 6 months and prioritizes latency predictability, Dedicated is likely the most economical path. If you want to keep flexibility and avoid legal commitments, start Hosted and migrate to Dedicated once monthly usage stabilizes — we can provide hybrid routing so critical traffic uses Dedicated and lower-priority traffic falls back to Hosted.

Action items I will take:
- Prepare a detailed 12-month TCO spreadsheet and a sample reserve schedule by Wed, May 5.
- Pull sample SLA language and SOC2 evidence to share with procurement.

Ben — if you have any pricing levers (market credits or onboarding discounts) worth offering to expedite a decision, flag them here and I can align with Olivia.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment selection & cost follow-up (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Olivia / Team — quick note from procurement/discount side. We can offer a structured 12-month commit with the following optional levers to help the total cost:
- Signing credit: one-month hosted credit to offset migration/onboarding costs.
- Ramp schedule: tiered commit where initial 3 months are at 60% of committed baseline to reduce early-stage overcommit risk.
- Annual price protection: fixed unit rates for 12 months with a 3% cap on increases for multi-year deals.

If Streamline can share a target committed baseline (e.g., 250M tokens/mo), I can draft an indicative commercial term sheet and a preliminary SOW for Private evaluation if procurement requests it.

Olivia — happy to hop on a short call with your procurement on Friday to run through SOC2 + audit access and the ramp schedule.

Thanks,
Ben
